subject: Urgent: SSE streaming p99 spike during peak (LiveDesk production)
messages:
From: Marta Ruiz <marta@livedesk.io>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, support@redwood.com
Cc: LiveDesk Ops <ops@livedesk.io>
Date: Thu, 12 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Realtime SSE p99 spike during morning peak — urgent

Hi Vivek / Redwood team,

We're seeing a hard spike in p99 for the SSE streaming chat endpoint during our morning peak (09:00–09:30 PDT). Dashboard attached. Quick summary: p95 moved from ~210ms to ~1.2s and p99 from ~640ms to ~5.2s. Error-rate (502/504) also ticked up to ~1.8% from ~0.1%.

Impact: multiple chat sessions experienced stalls and reconnects; two customers reported dropped messages. This is affecting our SLA and we're getting noise internally.

What we captured:
- Sample trace IDs: 2ef4a9b0, 2ef4a9f2, 2ef4aa7c (included in livedesk_trace_ids.txt)
- Grafana link: https://redwood.grafana.net/d/abcd1234/sse-p99?orgId=1
- Attached: grafana_p99_20280412.png, sse_logs_20280412.tar.gz

Can someone escalate and confirm whether this is a runtime regression or capacity/traffic pattern? We are on the hosted API (route: "livedesk-prod-sse") and saw the spike across 3 AZs. Please advise immediate mitigations (routing to polling, fallback endpoints, or config changes).

--
Marta Ruiz
Ops Lead, LiveDesk
ops@livedesk.io

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta@livedesk.io>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Apr 2028 09:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Realtime SSE p99 spike during morning peak — urgent

Thanks Marta — we see the Grafana alert and the traces. I'm escalating to SRE and the runtime team now (cc'd).

Immediate ask for your ops team:
- Please forward the exact client-side timestamps for the three trace IDs you listed (both client send and client receive).
- If possible, flip debug logging for one affected instance for 10 minutes and share the log bundle (we've received sse_logs_20280412.tar.gz, thank you).

Immediate mitigations we'll try:
1) Route 20% of traffic for route "livedesk-prod-sse" to a conservative model variant (lower memory, lower kv cache pressure) as a canary.
2) Temporarily increase the socket-worker autoscale target by +30% to absorb bursts.
3) Enable prefix/KV caching for the route (if not already enabled) to reduce repeated KV cache thrash.

Connor/Hannah/Markus — can you confirm the plan and whether we can flip (1) + (2) ASAP? Also want a quick hypothesis on whether this is a runtime regression (kernel selection / quantization) vs workload pattern (sequence length spike).

I'll update Marta within 20–30 minutes.

--
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marta Ruiz <marta@livedesk.io>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Apr 2028 09:39:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Realtime SSE p99 spike during morning peak — urgent

On Thu, Apr 12, 2028 at 09:25 AM Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com> wrote:
> Connor/Hannah/Markus — can you confirm the plan and whether we can flip (1) + (2) ASAP? Also want a quick hypothesis on whether this is a runtime regression (kernel selection / quantization) vs workload pattern (sequence length spike).

Quick triage update: we've pulled spans for the IDs Marta provided. Observations:
- Frontend socket workers show increasing accept queue length and stalls between the socket accept and enqueue to the inference queue (~40–60ms additional).
- Inference backend shows a spike in KV cache eviction activity correlated with sequences that jumped from median 64 tokens to a burst at ~512 tokens for a 10 minute window — that increases KV cache churn and serialization overhead.
- We do not see new kernels being selected; kernel selection trace looks identical to baseline. That points away from a nightly runtime deploy regression.

Hypothesis: workload pattern (sudden long-sequence bursts) causing KV cache pressure -> eviction thrash -> increased per-request latency -> queueing at socket workers -> p99 spike.

Planned action (now):
- Apply canary routing: 20% traffic -> smaller model variant (can be reverted instantly).
- Increase socket-worker replicas by 35% for the route and relax the enqueue backpressure threshold for 15 minutes.
- Enable prefix/KV caching for this route and enable stricter LRU thresholds (should reduce eviction storm).

I'll apply the routing and scaling change now and report metrics in ~10 mins. If that doesn't improve, next step is to temporarily route traffic to gateway fallback (polling) for the most active org IDs.

--
Connor O'Brien
SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta@livedesk.io>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Apr 2028 09:56:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Realtime SSE p99 spike during morning peak — urgent

On Thu, Apr 12, 2028 at 09:39 AM Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com> wrote:
> I'll apply the routing and scaling change now and report metrics in ~10 mins.

Update for Marta: we've rolled the canary (20% -> smaller variant) and bumped socket worker replicas +35% in the three impacted AZs. We also enabled prefix caching and tightened LRU thresholds for the KV cache.

Initial results (09:50 PDT):
- p99 for route sampled at reduced level: from ~5.2s -> ~1.1s (customer-facing aggregated p99 for a 5 minute window).
- Error-rate dropped from ~1.8% -> 0.4%.
- We still see occasional reconnections from ~2–3% of sessions (likely client timeouts during the worst of the spike).

Asking LiveDesk: can you confirm whether you still see user-visible issues or whether reconnects have subsided? We'll keep the canary live for 60 more minutes while we continue to monitor.

--
Hannah Schmitt
SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Marta Ruiz <marta@livedesk.io>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: LiveDesk Ops <ops@livedesk.io>
Date: Thu, 12 Apr 2028 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Realtime SSE p99 spike during morning peak — urgent

Thanks for the quick action — the dashboard looks much improved. We still see intermittent reconnects during 09:05–09:40 (about ~2% of sessions) but dropped requests are down. Attached a small log bundle with client timestamps (livedesk_trace_ids.txt) and the full logs (sse_logs_20280412.tar.gz).

One ask from our side: we would like a short post-incident note that explains the root cause and what permanent mitigation you plan to prevent recurrence (e.g., KV cache tuning, model-variant routing rules, or guardrails on sequence length). Our product leadership is asking about SLA credits if this meets the SLA breach threshold.

--
Marta Ruiz
Ops Lead, LiveDesk
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Marta Ruiz <marta@livedesk.io>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Apr 2028 15:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Exec summary requested — LiveDesk SSE incident (morning peak)

Team — please provide a short executive summary for the war room: 3 bullets on what happened, impact to the customer, and proposed next steps (timeline + owner). Also include whether this is a product/runtime change we should prioritize or a customer workload pattern we should defend against. Marta, please include any downstream customer impacts you need captured for SLA consideration.

I want a one-page summary by EOD and a proposed follow-up meeting for a postmortem next week. If we need to offer credits, include an estimate for the finance team.

Thanks — this looks like a clear example of workload-driven KV-cache pressure that needs a durable mitigation.

--
Lauren Bishop
VP, Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
